_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Early Peoples and Iron Age
910.label: Event
910.description: Hunter-gatherer communities; Bantu and Nilotic migrations; development of iron-working and agricultural societies in the Great Lakes region.

910.name: Early Hunter-Gatherer Communities
910.label: Event
910.description: Batwa and other hunter-gatherer communities; Stone Age sites in western Uganda; forest-dwelling peoples.

910.name: Bantu and Nilotic Migrations
910.label: Event
910.description: Bantu-speaking peoples arrive from west; Nilotic (Luo, Acholi, Langi) and Nilo-Hamitic peoples from the north; iron smelting traditions.

920.name: Great Lakes Kingdoms
920.label: Event
920.description: Rise of Bunyoro-Kitara empire; emergence of Buganda, Ankole, Toro, and Busoga kingdoms; cattle and banana-based civilisations.

920.name: Bunyoro-Kitara Empire
920.label: Event
920.description: Bunyoro-Kitara as dominant Great Lakes kingdom; Bachwezi dynasty legends; control of salt, iron, and cattle.

920.name: Rise of Buganda Kingdom
920.label: Event
920.description: Buganda emerges as tributary of Bunyoro; gradually expands; kabaka (king) centralised power; maritime control of Lake Victoria.

930.name: Buganda Expansion and European Exploration
930.label: Event
930.description: Buganda becomes dominant power; Arab trade contacts; Speke and Baker seek source of the Nile; religious wars.

930.name: Buganda Dominance
930.label: Event
930.description: Buganda supplants Bunyoro as regional power; standing army; sophisticated administrative system; Arab trade in guns and cloth.

930.name: Speke and Baker: Source of the Nile
930.label: Event
930.description: John Hanning Speke reaches Lake Victoria 1858; identifies source of the Nile; Samuel Baker discovers Lake Albert.

940.name: British Protectorate
940.label: Event
940.description: Imperial British East Africa Company; Uganda Agreement 1900; Buganda privileged position; cotton and coffee economy; path to independence.

940.name: IBEAC and Early British Control
940.label: Event
940.description: Imperial British East Africa Company; Lugard arrives 1890; British protectorate declared 1894.

940.name: Uganda Agreement 1900
940.label: Event
940.description: Agreement between Britain and Buganda; mailo land system; Buganda chiefs become landed gentry; indirect rule.

950.name: Post-Independence Turmoil
950.label: Event
950.description: Obote's centralisation; Idi Amin's reign of terror; Tanzanian invasion; second Obote regime; Bush War; Museveni victory.

950.name: Obote First Government
950.label: Event
950.description: Milton Obote PM then president; abolishes kingdoms 1967; 'Move to the Left'; Buganda crisis; increasing authoritarianism.

950.name: Idi Amin's Reign of Terror
950.label: Event
950.description: Idi Amin seizes power; expulsion of 80,000 Asians 1972; State Research Bureau; estimated 100,000-500,000 killed; Entebbe raid 1976.

960.name: Museveni Era and Modern Uganda
960.label: Event
960.description: NRM governance; economic recovery; HIV/AIDS response; LRA insurgency; oil discovery; multiparty transition; democratic backsliding.

960.name: NRM Economic Reconstruction
960.label: Event
960.description: Museveni stabilises economy; 'no-party' Movement system; structural adjustment; praised as 'new breed' African leader.

960.name: HIV/AIDS Response
960.label: Event
960.description: Uganda's early and effective HIV/AIDS response; prevalence drops from 15% to 5%; ABC campaign; global model.
